title: Finite-coefficient exceptional adjunction and coefficient mates over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\geq1$. For a finite coefficient ring $A$ occurring below, let $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ mean the full stable enhanced subcategory of the derived category of $A_T$-module sheaves with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, admitting etale-origin witnesses on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and put $F_A=Rg_{*,A}j_!$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. For $T=X,Y$, let $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $f_A^\times$ be the ordinary etale right adjoint of $Rg_{\mathrm{et},*,A}j_{\mathrm{et},!}$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], with its unit and counit. On the etale-origin finite constructible subcategory define
$$G_A=Rf_A^!=\nu_X^* f_A^\times R\nu_{Y,*}.$$
The adjunction on this subcategory is transported using the site-comparison unit and the compact-support comparison [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison, lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. This construction is made for the arbitrary field $k$ just specified.

The functors $F_A,G_A$ preserve these finite-Tor constructible categories and $F_A\dashv G_A$ there, with the geometric finite-coefficient units $\eta_A$ and counits $\epsilon_A$. Consider either a quotient $A_m\to A_n$, $m\ge n$, or the finite-free map $R/t^n\to S/t^nS$ for a finite extension $E\subset F$ with valuation ring $S=\mathcal O_F$. Put $T_X=-\otimes_A^L B_X$ and $T_Y=-\otimes_A^L B_Y$ for the corresponding coefficient extensions. The canonical projection comparison
$$q_{A,B}:T_YF_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_X$$
is an equivalence of enhanced functors on $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Its right-adjoint mate
$$b_{A,B}:T_XG_A\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BT_Y$$
is an equivalence on $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Specifically, $b_{A,B}$ is the $F_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $T_Y\epsilon_A\circ q_{A,B,G_A}^{-1}$; consequently
$$\epsilon_B\circ F_B(b_{A,B})=T_Y\epsilon_A\circ q_{A,B,G_A}^{-1}.$$
For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ the unit identity is
$$G_B(q_{A,B,K})\circ b_{A,B,F_AK}\circ T_X(\eta_{A,K})=\eta_{B,T_XK}.$$ The geometric models for $F_A$ and the maps $q$ are the enhanced open-extension/proper-direct-image models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; their tensor associativity, identity, coefficient-composition and compactification-refinement diagrams are coherent. The mates $b$ have the same identities and coherences. These assertions also hold for the mixed diagrams obtained by composing the displayed coefficient maps. Thus extension from $R$ to $S$ compares the whole exceptional coefficient system, including its counit, on the cofinal quotients $S/t^nS$; these are the subsequence $S/v^{en}$ for a uniformizer $v$ of $S$ and ramification index $e$. No integral inverse-limit adjunction, rational or condensed comparison is asserted.

source.place: Finite-stage counit-normalized coefficient comparison, extended from its smooth chart case to arbitrary separated finite-type k-morphisms by closed-support triangles and local affine embeddings; enhanced and finite-free system clauses are agent-written supplements.

proof.text: Work first on ordinary etale sites. All schemes in a compactification are finite type over k and hence Noetherian: apply finite-type-over-Noetherian to Spec(k), whose only ideals are 0 and k. The coefficient rings A_n are finite local rings by the DVR and finite-quotient statements. For E contained in F, uniqueness of the extending absolute value identifies the restriction from F with the absolute value on E, so R is a subring of S and |t|_F<1. The DVR expansion in S writes t=u v^e with u a unit and e>=1; hence t^nS=v^{en}S, and S/tS is finite by the finite-quotient statement. Here is the missing finite-generation argument, rather than an invocation of a geometric coefficient lemma. Choose representatives b_1,...,b_h in S for all elements of S/tS. Starting with x_0=x in S, recursively choose i_r with x_r=b_{i_r}+t x_{r+1}. Then x=sum_{r<N}t^r b_{i_r}+t^N x_N, and |t^N x_N|_F<=|t|_F^N tends to zero. For each i, the partial coefficient sums sum_{r<N,i_r=i}t^r are Cauchy in E; completeness gives a limit a_i in the closed unit ball R. Taking limits in the finite sum gives x=sum_i a_i b_i. Thus S is finitely generated over R, and it is torsion-free since R and S lie in fields. The DVR finite-free lemma makes S finite free over R; reducing a finite basis gives B=S/t^nS finite free over A=R/t^n. The ideal identity above is independent of the units relating uniformizers. Thus every ring in the question is a positive DVR quotient, is finite Noetherian, and is annihilated by an ell-power invertible on every scheme here: apply the same positive-valuation expansion to ell in each valuation ring. Choose intervals with a<=b, enlarging an interval if necessary for a zero object.

proof.text: For any k-map h between finite-type k-schemes, lem-kun-0f10(1), interpreted by def-kun-cd, supplies a finite c with R^q h_* M=0 for q>c for all torsion abelian sheaves. The restriction-of-scalars comparison, applied to Z \to A, transfers this bound to A-module sheaves; the forgetful functor is exact and detects zero objects. In particular this applies to the proper map g and to every complementary open j used below. No assumption on the absolute cohomological dimension of k is made. For bounded inputs, the bound implies Rh_* sends cohomological [a,b] into [a,b+c]: filter by the finitely many cohomology truncations, use Rh_*(M[-r])=Rh_*M[-r], and the long exact cohomology sequences of those triangles.

proof.text: Rh_* preserves ordinary bounded constructible finite-Tor complexes for these h and DVR stages A. Indeed thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility gives bounded constructibility. If K has Tor amplitude [a,b], use lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible to represent K by flat constructible terms in [a,b]. Tensoring those terms with any finite A-algebra B gives flat constructible B-module sheaves in the same degrees: on a common finite constructible stratification their fibres are finite modules, and B-flatness follows from (P tensor_A B) tensor_B N=P tensor_A N. In particular K tensor_A^L kappa is bounded constructible in [a,b]. Since kappa is a finitely presented A-module and K belongs to D^-, lem-sf-projection-finite-constant and Step 2 identify (Rh_*K) tensor_A^L kappa with Rh_*(K tensor_A^L kappa). Its cohomology vanishes outside [a,b+c]. Apply lem-exc-residue-tor-test on the target to obtain Tor amplitude [a,b+c]. The same argument with M=B in the projection lemma gives the canonical coefficient comparison T Rh_* K \to Rh_* T K as an isomorphism after restriction of B-scalars. The restriction-of-scalars comparison identifies the target with the B-linear direct image; restriction detects isomorphisms, so this is the B-linear projection isomorphism itself, for both coefficient maps in the question.

proof.text: For an open immersion j, exact extension by zero preserves bounded constructibility: extend a constructibility stratification on its open domain by the closed complement, on which the sheaf is zero. Its stalks are the original stalks or zero. Consequently extension by zero takes a flat constructible model to a flat constructible model of the same length, and the natural map T j_! \to j_! T is an isomorphism: use a flat model and check its termwise tensor map on stalks. Conservativity of geometric stalks proves isomorphism of this specified map. Composing with Step 3 for g proves that F_A^et=Rg_*j_! preserves D^b_ctf and that its canonical projection comparison q is invertible. This is the projection comparison built by the geometric open/proper operations, not a newly chosen isomorphism.

source.place: Extension by zero and its geometric stalks; termwise flat-model argument followed by proper direct image

proof.text: The ambient etale adjoint f_A^times exists by thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint. Use the unbounded compactification and composition comparisons of lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons; every map here is separated of finite type between Noetherian schemes. For the local factors and their composites, thm-nagata-compactification gives compactifiability: the targets are quasi-compact and quasi-separated (they are separated finite-type k-schemes). Transposing its left-functor composition isomorphism by the two ambient adjunctions identifies (gf)^times with f^times g^times on the whole ordinary derived categories, with the composite unit and counit. Thus this use of composition does not presuppose that an exceptional image is bounded below. Source-open locality is precisely the canonical isomorphism of lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality. For an open target restriction v, v_! dashv v^* and the same composition comparison give the corresponding v^* factor in the right adjoint. All these identifications use conjugate adjunctions and the mate-pasting identities, so their units and counits have fixed normalizations.

source.place: Tags 0F5Y and 0F7H–0F7L: ordinary-etale exceptional adjoint, compactification independence and composition; source-open locality via the cited node

proof.text: For a closed immersion i:Z\toP between finite-type k-schemes, its complementary open j is quasi-compact since P is Noetherian. Step 2 gives the uniform vanishing required by prop-exc-closed-tor. Theorem thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility, applied to j and a constructible sheaf in degree zero, gives constructibility of each R^qj_* of that sheaf. Thus every hypothesis of prop-exc-closed-tor holds, and i^times=Ri^! preserves D^b_ctf. For a projection pi:A^r_V\toV, thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity identifies pi^times L with pi^*L(r)[2r] by the adjoint of the stated trace. Exact inverse image preserves constructibility and flatness; the twist is locally constant and etale locally free of rank one by lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback, applied to m=ell^s annihilating A (m is invertible on these k-schemes). Hence this expression preserves D^b_ctf. Cover Y by finitely many affine V and each inverse image by finitely many affine U. Finite algebra generators give a closed immersion U\toA^r_V factoring f|U. By Step 5 and open adjunctions, u^* f^times L identifies with i^times pi^times v^*L, where u:U\toX and v:V\toY. The right side is bounded constructible finite-Tor. These properties glue across the finite open cover: take the minimum of the finitely many lower bounds and maximum of upper bounds, and glue the finite constructibility stratifications. Consequently f^times preserves D^b_ctf over the original arbitrary k.

proof.text: For any finite coefficient ring here, etale/pro-etale comparison identifies bounded etale constructible complexes with intrinsically constructible bounded pro-etale complexes. It also identifies their finite-Tor subcategories. In the forward direction, pull back a bounded flat constructible etale model: exactness of nu^* and the flat-term pullback assertion for ringed topoi give a bounded flat model on the pro-etale site. In the reverse direction, write K=nu^*K0 by constructible derived origin; if K has Tor amplitude [a,b], its tensor with the constant residue field has cohomology in [a,b]. Tensor-pullback compatibility identifies this with nu^*(K0 tensor_A^L kappa). Exactness and full faithfulness of nu^* on D^+ reflect this interval, so the residue-field Tor test shows that K0 has the same Tor amplitude. The etale origin is bounded, so all these uses of D^+ full faithfulness are legitimate. Apply compact-support site comparison to identify F_A nu_X^* with nu_Y^* F_A^et. It follows from Steps 4 and 6 that F_A and G_A=nu_X^* f_A^times Rnu_{Y,*} preserve the stated pro-etale category. For K=nu_X^*K0 and L=nu_Y^*L0 the Hom chain Hom(F_A K,L)=Hom(F_A^et K0,L0)=Hom(K0,f_A^times L0)=Hom(K,G_A L) gives the required adjunction. Each equality uses the specified comparison and unit, so its unit and counit are precisely the transported geometric ones. Tensor-pullback compatibility transports the specified q of Step 4 as well.

source.place: finite etale/pro-etale duality and site-comparison transport

proof.text: For an affine-space projection pi:A^r_V\toV, apply det-sp-reduction-exceptional to the smooth morphism pi and the map A\toB. Its statement covers every map of finite commutative ell-primary rings, so it covers both the nonflat quotient A_m\toA_n and the finite-free R/t^n\toS/t^nS. It says that the counit-transposed coefficient comparison for pi is invertible, and specifies its chart value as the canonical tensor reassociation of pi^*(-)(r)[2r]. This is the current blueprint's Kummer/projective-line construction, not a conclusion that arbitrary mates of isomorphisms are isomorphisms. Identify the finite pro-etale compact-support functor in that node with our F_pi: both are Rg_*j_! for the same standard compactification. The coefficient comparison used there is b of det-sp-reduction-direct-image. Its statement defines the proper part as the counit transpose after coefficient extension, followed by the open-extension tensor comparison, so it is exactly our pro-etale q. Separately, lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate says that the etale/pro-etale direct-image comparison is the specified site-comparison counit transpose. Together with tensor-pullback compatibility, mate-pasting, and the open/proper compact-support comparison, this identifies the site-transport of the ordinary-etale q of Step 4 with that same pro-etale q: transposing either composite leaves the same proper counit tensored with B, followed by the same open-extension tensor map. The right adjoint in Step 7 and the finite right adjoint in det-sp-reduction-exceptional are right adjoints of this same functor on the full bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories. Uniqueness of right adjoints gives the unique counit-preserving identification between them. Under this identification the defining equation for the comparison is exactly epsilon_B F_B(b_pi)=T epsilon_A q_pi^{-1}; injectivity of the adjunction transpose therefore identifies the invertible comparison with b_pi. This proves the projection case on the pro-etale constructible category. To obtain the ordinary-etale assertion used for the local factorization in Step 10, transport through the finite constructible site equivalences of Step 7. Tensor-pullback compatibility carries T to T, compact-support site comparison carries F to F, and the transported Hom bijection carries the actual counits and their transposes to one another. Thus it carries the ordinary-etale b_pi to this pro-etale comparison, and full faithfulness reflects its invertibility. The case r=0 is the identity adjunction and tensor reassociation.

source.place: Charts and uniqueness of counit transposes, applied only to the smooth affine-space factor; ordinary-etale transport is supplied explicitly here.

proof.text: For a closed immersion i with open complement j, use the canonical enhanced support triangle i_*i^times L \to L \to Rj_*j^*L. Tensor it with B and compare with the B-coefficient support triangle of TL. The middle map is the identity. The right map is the canonical coefficient projection of Step 3, hence invertible; its square with the middle map commutes because the second arrow is the unit of j^* dashv Rj_* and the projection comparison is its tensor transpose. The left map is the canonical map of fibres in the enhanced stable category. Identify T i_* with i_* T: a closed immersion is proper, so Step 3 supplies its coefficient projection (indeed i_* is exact in the support triangle). The resulting left map is an isomorphism by triangle two-out-of-three. Its composite to the middle term equals T epsilon_i by construction of that fibre map. Therefore, after the comparison T i_*=i_*T, it is i_* of the specified adjunction mate b_i. The identity i^*i_*=id shows that i_* detects isomorphisms on complexes. This identity for module sheaves follows from lem-kun-04ca: the left-inverse isomorphism for abelian sheaves respects the A-action by its naturality for scalar multiplications; exactness of i_* and i^* extends it to complexes. Thus b_i is invertible. The fibre construction is essential here: an arbitrary completion of a square to a triangle would not identify the required mate.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.18, proof: closed-immersion support triangle and Lemma 6.7.17; the specified enhanced fibre map identifies the counit mate.

proof.text: The projection comparisons for a composite of geometric maps are the composites of the projection comparisons of the factors. To verify this equality, transpose both maps under pullback/direct-image adjunctions: both become the pullback of the input tensored with B followed by the same two direct-image counits; tensor associativity and the triangle identities identify them. The same calculation for open extension uses its counit, and for a compactification refinement uses the proper/open comparison built from those same units and counits. This proves coefficient compatibility of the compactification and composition isomorphisms of lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons. Applying mate-pasting now identifies the coefficient mate for a composite with the pasted mates of its factors and identifies its restriction on each affine U of Step 6 with the composite of b_i, b_pi, and the coefficient identity for v^*. The last identity follows directly from exact pullback commuting with coefficient tensor. Source locality identifies this restriction with u^*b_f, with the adjunctions transported as in Step 5. Steps 8 and 9 make it invertible on each U. Its cone has zero cohomology on an open cover, hence zero geometric stalks; geometric-stalk conservativity applied to the cohomology sheaves proves b_f invertible. Via Step 7 this proves invertibility of the exact b_{A,B} in the question for quotient maps. The same argument proves it for the finite-free map because Step 3, the smooth coefficient-mate comparison of Step 8 and the support triangle also apply to that map. Alternatively for the finite-free map choose an A-basis of B: both T and q identify with the same finite direct sum, and the right-adjoint mate is that finite-sum identification by counit naturality. This alternative is only a check; the defined b is basis-independent.

proof.text: The counit identity is the defining equation for the transpose b, so holds as an equality of the specified maps. For the unit equation, let alpha=G_B(q_K) b_{F_A K} T_X(eta_{A,K}). Its F_B dashv G_B transpose is epsilon_{B,F_BT_XK} F_B(alpha). Counit naturality moves q_K to the outside, and the defining counit equation for b changes this expression to q_K (T_Y epsilon_{A,F_AK}) q^{-1}_{G_AF_AK} F_BT_X(eta_{A,K}). Naturality of q changes the last two factors to T_YF_A(eta_{A,K}) q_K^{-1}. The A-triangle identity now reduces the whole composite to q_K id q_K^{-1}=id. The transpose of id is eta_{B,T_XK}, proving exactly the displayed unit equation. This is elementary adjunction algebra, using no invertibility principle for mates.

proof.text: Use the simultaneous enhanced geometric models of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections for tensor, exact open extension, proper direct image, site inverse image, and the specified projection/adjunction transposes. Their evaluations give the operations used above; since a morphism in these models is an equivalence exactly when its component is, the q isomorphisms already proved are enhanced equivalences. The tensor associativity coherence for A\toB\toC, including a quotient followed by a finite-free map or the reverse mixed square, is the coherence of K-flat tensor composition; both projection composites have the same counit transpose as checked in Step 10. Identity, composition, and refinement diagrams use these specified geometric constructions and their coherence homotopies. Once the ordinary right adjoints preserve the full stable subcategories and the specified mates are invertible, apply lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates to their coefficient towers to obtain enhanced right-adjoint realizations with those exact units/counits. A constant tower gives the individual enhanced adjunction; any coefficient arrow and any finite composable string can be padded by identities to such a tower. Naturality for coherent transformations and mate-pasting give the same enhanced coherences for b, including the mixed diagrams. Here the node is used only for finite evaluations and their specified section maps, not for an inverse-limit adjunction. It asserts precisely this enhancement under invertible mates; we have verified that hypothesis rather than assumed an enhancement of an arbitrary homotopy-category transformation.

source.place: Enhanced coefficient-system supplement using the separately cited semilinear section and adjoint-mate recognition statements; no inverse limit is used

proof.text: Finally Step 1 writes t=u v^e with u in S^times and e>=1, so t^nS=v^{en}S and S/t^nS=S/v^{en}S as quotient rings; the cited DVR and finite-quotient statements make these precisely the finite local coefficient stages. The finite-free lemma applies using the finite-generation and torsion-free hypotheses proved explicitly in Step 1, and reducing its basis gives the finite-free extensions at each level. Given any positive integer r, choose n>=r; then en>=r. Thus the indices en form a cofinal subsystem, and all coefficient, unit and counit comparisons just proved restrict to it. This is only an assertion about finite coefficient systems; no passage to inverse limits or extension to rational or condensed coefficient categories has occurred.

split_report.summary: Thirteen-step arbitrary-field finite-coefficient proof using existing nodes only. Replaced the inherited large finite-field coefficient-extension citation by the DVR, finite-quotient, and DVR finite-free algebra facts; retained the current smooth coefficient-mate theorem on affine-space factors, identified the exact counit-normalized mates through site comparison and uniqueness, then used closed-support triangles and local affine embeddings for arbitrary f. Corrected the restriction-of-scalars map to Z -> A and removed the obsolete torsion-trace route. On repair re-reading, supplied an explicit finite-generation proof for S over R using finite S/tS and completeness, and cited the existing absolute-value uniqueness and completeness leaves. The local closed/smooth coefficient argument is sourced to Bhatt–Scholze 6.7.17–18 with current-blueprint smooth input.
